chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Taxonomy of Alternative Data

lessons.title: Transaction and Payment Data: UPI, Credit Card Panels, and Consumption Proxies

body.text: Transaction data is the closest thing to ground truth in this course, actual money actually moving, but the rawest version of it mixes real consumption with transfers that have nothing to do with demand at all.

children.text: Web traffic and satellite imagery are proxies, inferences about activity from an indirect signal. Payment data is different: it records the actual transaction. That makes it, in principle, the most direct consumption signal in this course. It also means getting it wrong is more embarrassing, because the mistake is usually not noticing that you have mixed genuine spending with something that only looks like spending on the surface.
Three Ways to Observe Money Moving

children.text: The P2P vs P2M Trap in UPI Data

markDefs.definition: Person-to-Person: a UPI transfer between two individuals, such as splitting a restaurant bill, paying rent, or sending money to family. It reflects money movement, not a purchase of goods or services.
Person-to-Merchant: a UPI payment made to a registered business for goods or services, the transaction type that actually reflects consumer demand.

children.text: NPCI's headline UPI numbers report total transaction count and value across the entire system, and that total bundles together

payments. If you treat total UPI value growth as a consumption growth signal without separating the two, you are letting rent payments, peer transfers, and bill-splitting move your 'demand' indicator just as much as an actual increase in retail spending. A researcher who has not made this adjustment is not measuring consumption, they are measuring how comfortable India has become with digital payments in general, which is a different and much less useful question for a trading signal.

cards.definition: A UPI transfer between individuals, such as rent or splitting a bill. Reflects money movement, not consumption.
A UPI payment made to a registered business. The transaction type that actually reflects consumer demand.
A standardized code identifying the type of business a card transaction was made with, such as dining, travel, or apparel, allowing spend to be split by sector.

body.title: Choosing the Right UPI Metric
body.question: You want to build an early indicator of retail consumption growth using UPI data. Which metric should you prioritize?
options: Total UPI transaction value across all categories
Total UPI transaction count across all categories
P2M transaction value specifically, with P2P transfers excluded
The ratio of UPI transactions to total bank account holders
body.explanation: Only P2M transactions represent payments to merchants for goods and services. Total value or count across all categories mixes in P2P transfers, rent payments, and peer-to-peer activity that can grow independently of actual consumption, contaminating the signal you are trying to build.

children.text: Card Spend Panels and Merchant Category Codes

Card networks tag every transaction with a Merchant Category Code, a standardized identifier for the type of business involved. Aggregated and anonymized at the category level, this lets a researcher watch specific discretionary categories rather than blunt, economy-wide totals.

Receipt and Order Panels: A Thinner Layer in India, For Now

In more mature alternative data markets, vendors build detailed order-level panels by parsing opted-in consumers' structured e-commerce email receipts, giving a line-item view of what people actually bought. This category is thinner in India today: a large share of order and delivery confirmations arrive through SMS or app notifications rather than structured email receipts, which makes them harder to parse at scale. This is consistent with the pattern from Chapter 1, India's alternative data vendor layer is newer and less dense, so expect this specific sub-category to mature over the next few years rather than assume it already offers the same coverage it does in the US.

body.title: Why payment data carries extra regulatory weight in India

children.text: Payment data is financial data about identifiable people by its very nature, which puts it squarely inside India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the same way individual-level geolocation data did in the previous lesson. It carries one more layer beyond that: the RBI's 2018 circular on storage of payment system data requires payment system operators to store the full data related to payment systems in India, which shapes how any vendor or bank can even structure a data-sharing arrangement in the first place. Any panel your desk uses must already be aggregated and anonymized well before it reaches you, never something you anonymize yourself after receiving raw records.

body.title: A Suspiciously Specific Data Offer
body.scenario: A vendor offers your desk a 'premium panel' that includes individual UPI transaction records with masked but consistently trackable customer identifiers, claiming this lets you build household-level spending cohorts for sharper consumption signals than any aggregate panel could offer.
body.prompt: What is wrong with this offer, independent of how useful the resulting signal might be?
body.modelAnswer: A consistently trackable identifier, even if the name itself is masked, still allows individual behaviour to be reconstructed and re-identified over time, which is exactly the kind of processing India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, is built to govern, and it sits well outside the aggregated, anonymized standard that legitimate payment panels are expected to meet. Combined with the RBI's data localization and payment system data storage requirements, a vendor offering trackable individual-level UPI records, regardless of how the product is marketed, should be treated as a serious compliance red flag rather than a superior data product. The correct response is the same one used throughout this course: route it to legal and compliance before any commercial conversation continues, and expect the likely answer to be no.

body.text: The single most valuable adjustment in this entire lesson is boring: filter P2P out of UPI data before you call anything a consumption signal. Advanced researchers lose more time chasing sophisticated models on a contaminated input than they would spend just cleaning the input properly first.

Companies named in this lesson illustrate sector examples only, and the dining index versus same-store-sales chart is a hypothetical pattern, not reported data for any specific chain. Nothing here is a recommendation to trade any security. Always route payment and transaction data sourcing through legal and compliance review given RBI and DPDP Act requirements.

points: Transaction data records actual money movement rather than inferring activity, making it the most direct consumption proxy in this course, but also the easiest to misread if not filtered correctly
NPCI's monthly UPI data bundles P2P transfers with P2M merchant payments, and only the P2M share reflects actual consumption
Card spend panels tagged by Merchant Category Code let you watch specific discretionary categories, such as dining, travel, and apparel, ahead of the sectors' quarterly results

A leading relationship between a card panel index and a company's later-reported same-store-sales growth is exactly the kind of informational edge worth testing formally, not just eyeballing on a chart
Receipt and order panels are a thinner category in India today than in mature markets like the US, largely due to SMS and app-based order confirmations rather than structured email receipts
Payment data carries extra regulatory weight in India: it is personal data under the DPDP Act, 2023, and is also shaped by the RBI's payment system data storage and localization requirements
Any vendor offering individually trackable transaction records, however the identifiers are described, is a compliance red flag regardless of how strong the resulting signal might be
